subject.title: fix(channels): honor configured read target policies

question: Should OpenClaw adopt host-attested current-turn identity plus channel-owner fail-closed target policy as the canonical authorization contract for bundled and external plugin tool paths?
rationale: The code is coherent, but it intentionally changes trusted authority, public plugin context, accepted targets, and provider action availability; automation cannot choose that permanent compatibility and security contract.

options.title: Adopt the contract
options.body: Reconstruct the patch on current main, preserve host-owned authority, and require refreshed exact-head upgrade and provider proof.

options.title: Narrow the first landing
options.body: Land core attestation and selected bundled-channel enforcement first while separately designing the external plugin compatibility seam.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Pause if maintainers do not intend configured policy to fail closed for previously provider-accessible targets and actions.

recommendation.title: Adopt the contract
recommendation.body: Reconstruct the patch on current main, preserve host-owned authority, and require refreshed exact-head upgrade and provider proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current history across plugin tool context, Codex integration, and central tool assembly, which are the contract's owner boundary.
